summary.en: The continuation of OSTQD extends its finite-dimensional framework to thermal open systems and conditional low-energy gravity models. It derives frozen-coefficient JT fluctuation cumulants and a smooth-band chiral-horizon obstruction, with separate checks of KMS covariance, greybody scattering and quantum-channel bottlenecks.

general.en: Follow the physical questions behind thermal baths, fluctuating black holes, horizon correlations, and information recovery.

student.en: Work through thermal channel equations, energy cumulants, point-split correlations, and controlled model comparisons.

expert.en: Examine the hypotheses, proof strategies, analytic obstructions, quantitative controls, and formalization boundaries.

en: The paper builds on the preceding finite-dimensional OSTQD study by relaxing strict subsystem energy conservation for reduced open systems. The guides cover SK normalization, KMS covariance and its time-dependent limits, Ward identities and JT fluctuation closures, bosonic and chiral-horizon diagnostics, per-port thermal locking, greybody scattering, and separated information benchmarks.

The focused analytical results are conditional: a specified free chiral-boson smooth-band defect and the frozen-coefficient JT cumulant closure. A positive global continuum state, a microscopic rate, observer-separated outcome instruments and a unified evaporation endpoint remain open.

web_figures.title: Thermal relaxation and non-secular dynamics
web_figures.description: Original manuscript Figure 1, F1–F2. In a six-level mode at fixed temperature, purity can rise during cooling while relative entropy and the symmetric GNS divergence decrease. The two-level unprojected Bloch–Redfield comparison tests complete positivity; these are calculated examples.

web_figures.title: JT evaporation and the linearized variance
web_figures.description: Original manuscript Figure 2, F3. For C=12, c=24, S₀=20 and T₀=1, the saddle and exact-step Gaussian simulation illustrate the fluctuation variance and distinct validity thresholds. Late-time curves are extrapolations, not controlled predictions of an endpoint.

web_figures.title: Cross-horizon coherence and detector prescriptions
web_figures.description: Original manuscript Figure 3, F4. Bosonic mode heating, the inverse-square point-split defect, and detector cutoff comparisons test distinct diagnostics. Smooth-band raw-cutoff finiteness does not imply a positive-type two-point function.

web_figures.title: Static absorption and a separate quantum-information model
web_figures.description: Original manuscript Figure 4, F5–F6. At fixed frequency the lowest partial-wave absorption cross sections shrink in the static Schwarzschild family; a separate eight-qubit diary model illustrates radiation and remnant recovery. These calculations do not identify a common gravitational endpoint.

# OSTQD–SK/JT research materials

**Consistency Audits of Observer-Separated Open Dynamics in 2D Dilaton Gravity: KMS Covariance, Non-Gaussian JT Fluctuations, and Chiral-Horizon Obstructions**

Yohtaro Soga · 27 November 2026

[Paper overview](../README.md) · [Reading guides](https://gawakkyu0603-bit.github.io/physics/en/quantum-gravity/ostqd-sk-jt/index.html) · [Preceding study](../../observer-separated-two-time-quantum-dynamics/README.md)

## Materials

| Resource | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [Manuscript (PDF)](paper/main.pdf) | 34 pages and 84 cited references. |
| [LaTeX source](paper/main.tex) · [Bibliography](paper/references.bib) · [Compilation instructions](paper/README.md) | Original source and four vector PDF figures. |
| [Lean project](lean4/README.md) · [Axiom check](lean4/OSTQD_SK/AxiomCheck.lean) · [Kernel log](lean4/VERIFICATION_LOG.txt) | 34 recorded machine-checked declarations; the formalized statements are distinguished from the continuum and physical arguments. |
| [Numerical code](scripts/verify_paper2_sk_jt.py) · [Recorded data](docs/numerical_verification.json) · [Requirements](scripts/requirements.txt) | Six numerical suites F1–F6, 258 recorded scientific numeric fields, seed 20261127. |
| [Prior literature](PRIOR_ART.md) · [Verification scope](VERIFICATION.md) | Equation-level attribution and the boundaries of the mathematical and numerical evidence. |
| [SHA-256 checksums](SHA256SUMS) · [Citation](CITATION.cff) | Original research-file identities and citation information. |

## Reproduction

Run on a working copy because the numerical program regenerates the figures and recorded data.

```sh
python -m pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python scripts/verify_paper2_sk_jt.py
```

With elan installed and the supplied Lean/Mathlib toolchain:

```sh
cd lean4
lake exe cache get
lake build OSTQD_SK
lake env lean OSTQD_SK/AxiomCheck.lean
```

For manuscript compilation, use [the LaTeX instructions](paper/README.md). See [verification scope](VERIFICATION.md) for assumptions, original execution details and analytic steps outside the formalization. The original files are kept unchanged; publication does not claim a new blanket license. Cite the actual manuscript using [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff).

# Consistency Audits of Observer-Separated Open Dynamics in 2D Dilaton Gravity

**KMS Covariance, Non-Gaussian JT Fluctuations, and Chiral-Horizon Obstructions**

Yohtaro Soga · 27 November 2026

This is the second study in the [OSTQD research series](../observer-separated-two-time-quantum-dynamics/README.md). It explicitly relaxes the preceding paper's strict subsystem energy-moment immunity for reduced thermal open systems. Its low-energy models are conditional and their physical completions remain open.

## Results and scope

| Result | Exact scope and material |
| --- | --- |
| **Fixed-temperature KMS covariance** | Eigenoperator jumps preserve two-time commutation despite energy exchange; detailed balance gives symmetric GNS decay. Time-dependent holonomy and Gibbs tracking require different controls. [Theorem 1 and Proposition 1](v1/paper/main.pdf), [Lean source](v1/lean4/OSTQD_SK/Theorem1_CovariantKMS.lean). |
| **JT fluctuations** | The frozen-coefficient linearized Bernard–Doyon closure has explicit cumulants for every order n≥2. State-dependent feedback changes the leading third cumulant. Three equilibrium closures with fixed drift give fourth-cumulant ratios 0.5, 1.5, 1.0. [Theorem 2 and Proposition 2](v1/paper/main.pdf), [Lean source](v1/lean4/OSTQD_SK/Theorem2_WardAndFDT.lean). |
| **Smooth-band chiral-horizon obstruction** | For nonzero smooth compactly supported number dephasing on the specified free chiral field, the raw tempered defect is non-Hadamard and its UV-finite raw detector response turns negative at large gap. Any positive-type finite-order point-contact extension requires a strictly positive contact coefficient and a high-gap floor. This does not establish existence of a global positive state. [Theorem 3 and Propositions 3–4](v1/paper/main.pdf), [Lean source](v1/lean4/OSTQD_SK/Theorem3_HorizonHadamard.lean). |
| **Thermal ports, greybody scattering, and channel erasure** | Per-port KMS locking, fixed-frequency static Schwarzschild asymptotics, exact replacer fidelity and separate finite models identify conditional restrictions, not a common gravitational endpoint. [Theorem 4 and Proposition 5](v1/paper/main.pdf), [Lean source](v1/lean4/OSTQD_SK/Theorem4_NonIsometricThroat.lean). |

[Manuscript (PDF)](v1/paper/main.pdf) · [Research materials](v1/README.md) · [Relation to prior literature](v1/PRIOR_ART.md) · [Mathematical and numerical verification scope](v1/VERIFICATION.md)

## English reading guides

[General readers](https://gawakkyu0603-bit.github.io/physics/en/quantum-gravity/ostqd-sk-jt/general.html) · [STEM students and graduates](https://gawakkyu0603-bit.github.io/physics/en/quantum-gravity/ostqd-sk-jt/student.html) · [Specialists](https://gawakkyu0603-bit.github.io/physics/en/quantum-gravity/ostqd-sk-jt/expert.html)

The preceding study is [Observer-Separated Two-Time Quantum Dynamics](../observer-separated-two-time-quantum-dynamics/README.md). Established open-system, gravity and quantum-information results are credited in the manuscript. The central new constructions are conditional analytic additions, not a derivation of microscopic gravity or a completed observer-separated instrument model.
